notes.title: THE DEADLY PATH – FAQ & COMMUNITY INFO
notes.content:
Hey Penitents,

[b]The Deadly Path[/b] has officially launched, and we are beyond grateful for your support! Whether you’ve been offering tributes, barely scraping through raids, or discovering new ways to (inevitably) perish, thank you for joining us on this cursed journey.

[h1]Leave us a Review – It Helps a Lot![/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44212693/8166da3a13aef543d0b6bf966f6f1cf9d86faac1.png[/img]

If you’re enjoying [b]The Deadly Path[/b], please consider leaving a [b]review on Steam[/b]. Your feedback means the world to us, and as a small indie team, it plays a huge role in supporting the game’s development and helping other players discover it.

Every review helps us grow, refine, and continue expanding [b]The Deadly Path[/b] - so let us know your thoughts!

[h2]👉 Leave a review here[/h2]
https://store.steampowered.com/app/2455350/The_Deadly_Path/

[h1]⚔️ THE DEADLY PATH – FAQ ⚔️
[/h1]
We’ve gathered some of the most frequently asked questions about [b]The Deadly Path[/b] to help you make the most of your time in the underworld. If you’ve got more questions, feel free to post them in the Steam discussions or [url=https://discord.gg/aeqeHm9uEJ]join our Discord community[/url]!

[h3]🕒 Is The Deadly Path launching in Early Access?[/h3]
👉 No - this is our full release! That said, we’ll still be continuing development post-launch with updates and fixes.

[h3]🎯 Will there be achievements?[/h3]
👉 Yes! There will be 18 achievements available at launch.

[h3]🕹️ Does The Deadly Path support Steam Deck?[/h3]
👉 We’re not Steam Deck Verified yet, but the game plays well on Deck thanks to our 16:10 resolution compatibility.

[h3]👥 Is there multiplayer or co-op?[/h3]
👉 No - The Deadly Path is a single-player experience, meticulously designed to let you face divine judgment all on your own.

[h3]📦 Will my progress carry over through updates?[/h3]
👉 Yes - we’ll avoid wiping progression where possible. If we do need to reset anything due to major changes, we’ll give you a heads-up.

[h3]🐛 How do I give feedback or report bugs?[/h3]
👉 We love hearing from you! Head over to our Discord and use the following channels:
• #feedback_and_suggestions – for ideas, balance, and general thoughts
• #bug-reports – for anything broken, cursed, or just plain weird
Also be sure to report any bugs to our online form you can find [url=https://fireshinegames.co.uk/customer_support/the-deadly-path/]HERE[/url]

[h3]💻 What platforms is The Deadly Path available on?[/h3]
👉 PC via Steam.

[h3]🎮 Will it come to consoles?[/h3]
👉 We'd love to explore bringing The Deadly Path to consoles in the future – for now, we're focused on making the PC version as good as it can be.

[h3]📹 Can I stream or make content about The Deadly Path?[/h3]
👉 Yes, yes, a thousand times yes. We love seeing your gameplay, chaos, and underworld-building tips. Tag us so we can share your creations!

[h3]📚 Is there lore I can read somewhere?[/h3]
👉 The gods are chatty and dramatic, so we’ll be sharing more lore via Steam blogs, in-game texts, and social posts. Keep your eyes peeled!

[h3]💀 What’s the actual goal of a run?[/h3]
👉 Survive the trials, manage your resources, build a thriving underworld settlement, and work towards completing the objectives set for you by your chosen deity.

[h3]🧱 Is there permanent progression?[/h3]
👉 Yes! Between runs, you can invest in upgrades using points earned by participating (successfully or not) in runs!

Thank you again for walking The Deadly Path with us. The gods are watching… and so are we. Stay tuned for future updates, and may your sacrifices be accepted!

– The Deadly Path Team

notes.title: Meet the Gods – Part 2
notes.content:
Greetings, Penitents.
Just when you thought you’d met the worst of them, the underworld has seen fit to introduce even more of it’s charmingly dreadful divine patrons. Whether you’re forging a path of glory or simply trying not to perish horribly, these gods are here to make things… interesting.
Let’s meet the next round of delightfully dreadful deities you’ll be trying to impress, appease, or simply survive.

[h1]EOCIDE[/h1]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44212693/f5809ddac2879c15dc991e7e0dcfdcbaa607bbb2.gif[/img]

Blood, sulk, and rage, bottled in a divine vessel with a flair for melodrama.
A headstrong god with ideas well above his station and the temper of a caffeinated wasp, Eocide is a living conduit for blood magic. His body is scrawled with primordial markings - a visual diary of poor life choices and unacknowledged genius. Worship him if you must, but don’t expect gratitude. He’s still bitter about not making the top spot in the pantheon’s popularity contest.

[h1]THE THING THAT GROWS[/h1]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44212693/a5a6c77db70c39184b3a49ba2490202ace6ca28d.gif[/img]

Half god, half compost heap, all fury.
Overlord of the Dread Pantheon, this fungal terror commands deference with the subtlety of a falling anvil. His shriveled, spore-ridden form radiates power and a general discontent with absolutely everything. Cross him, and you’ll be mulch before the day is out. Then again, even smiling at him funny seems to qualify as a slight, so good luck.

[h1]BRASS LEVIATHAN[/h1]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44212693/face25edb2eaa53d520d91862d2b271a15f33416.gif[/img]

Think ancient wrath meets eldritch grumble.
This enigmatic titan slumbers somewhere far below, seething in the abyss and muttering about the good old days. Its hulking brass form is less “majestic artifact” and more “forgotten horror that should probably stay buried.” But should it rise, expect chaos, destruction, and the distinct feeling that someone’s definitely getting blamed for waking it up.

[h1]MOTHER OF TEARS[/h1]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44212693/da9171867ccdc6e92ae74e732c72ac1cc499717f.gif[/img]

Tragedy personified - now with bonus wailing.
She is despair incarnate, a towering matriarch draped in sorrow and slightly questionable fashion choices. Equal parts corpse, crone, and catastrophic emotional baggage, the Mother of Tears isn’t so much worshipped as endured. Her dynasty needs restoring (apparently). Your involvement is mandatory. Bring tissues.

[h1]Join Us… If You Dare[/h1]

Each of these gods brings their own grotesque flavour to your run - new abilities, strategies, and, inevitably, fresh disasters. Whether you’re loyal to the Lord of Blight, whispering to rusted idols, or sobbing quietly under the weight of a fungal overlord’s disappointment, there’s something for everyone.

Don’t forget to join our [url=https://discord.gg/aeqeHm9uEJ]Discord[/url], where you can chat with other Penitents, share your best (and worst) strategies, or scream into the void about your latest run.

The Deadly Path launches March 25th – wishlist now, before one of the gods takes offence.
https://store.steampowered.com/app/2455350/The_Deadly_Path/

notes.title: The Gods of The Deadly Path - Part 1
notes.content:
Greetings, Penitents!

The gods are a truly charming bunch, aren’t they? Nothing quite like a pantheon composed of a walking biohazard, an overworked blacksmith of destruction, an existentially hungry void, and a giant corpse-eating fly to really set the mood.
If you’ve ever wondered what it’s like to serve deities that range from “[i]mildly concerning[/i]” to “[i]outright catastrophic[/i],” then you’re in luck. Today, we’re taking a closer look at some of the delightful patrons you’ll be grovelling before in [b]The Deadly Path[/b].

[h1]Roiann, The Blightcaster[/h1]
He from whom all manner of pestilence is borne - like a particularly unsanitary delivery service. Toil diligently, for [b]The Blightcaster[/b] is as likely to spare you as he is to take up knitting. A hideous amalgamation of cadaver and rodent ([i]both of whom are clearly regretting the merger[/i]), his skin pulsates with vile contagion, as if auditioning for the role of “[i]most horrifying biology experiment gone wrong.[/i]” Woe betide all who encounter the Lord of Disease, not least because he’s a very inconsiderate dinner guest.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44212693/cb30caf5598b03ed13c063eb4a08e7197fede860.gif[/img]

[h1]The One Who Rusts[/h1]
A vicious deity of [b]inconceivable strength[/b], she toils ceaselessly at the corrosive forges of fortune. Her [i]dreadborn hammer[/i] and tools produce only ruin, though one suspects her real talent lies in somehow making every project look like it was designed by a particularly ill-tempered architect on a bad day. If you believe in craftsmanship, she believes in its inevitable decay.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44212693/5e099ea93a4d60ef2357c11776488b41a841eaad.gif[/img]

[h1]The Maw[/h1]
A vile contradiction made flesh - or possibly something less appetizing. An incessant famine personified, it is intent on devouring all but the fabric of reality, leaving nothing but an awkward silence where existence used to be. The choice is simple: evolve its domain or become the main course. Either way, [b]The Maw[/b] dines tonight.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44212693/3c8f05c9e170efb0ed965159b53808cfffc2a285.gif[/img]

[h1]Bluebottle[/h1]
A repugnant deity whose grandmotherly form is merely an unsettling disguise for a grotesque, bloated [b]Bluebottle[/b]. [b]Winged, deadly[/b], and thoroughly [b]unpleasant at tea parties[/b], she spreads fear and panic wherever she goes, feasting on filth and hunting for fresh corpses like some sort of highly motivated waste management system. Pray you never catch her attention - she will follow you home.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44212693/51c3f6035b609c61a5d7ca3a9baff163c6d84642.gif[/img]

These are but a few of the divine horrors that lurk in [b]The Deadly Path[/b]. Each god has their own strengths, demands, and questionable personal hygiene habits. Who will you serve? Who will you defy? And more importantly... how long will you last?

[h2]The Deadly Path is coming soon![/h2]
Right then, Penitents - mark your calendars, set your alarms, and maybe carve the date into a particularly ominous-looking slab of stone. [b]The Deadly Path[/b] is [b]launching[/b] on [b]March 25th[/b], which means you’ve only got a few weeks left to mentally prepare for the horrors that await. Want to be the first to suffer? [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/2455350/The_Deadly_Path/]Wishlist now[/url], and Steam will kindly notify you the moment it’s available - like a concerned friend reminding you of an appointment you’re definitely not ready for.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2455350/The_Deadly_Path/

[h2]Join the Community[/h2]
The gods delight in watching your struggles - so why not share them with others? [url=url=https://discord.gg/aeqeHm9uEJ]Join our Discord[/url] to discuss strategies, trade suffering stories, and maybe even earn their favor (unlikely, but we can pretend).

🔗 [url=https://discord.gg/aeqeHm9uEJ]Join the Discord[/url]

Until next time, Penitents. May your offerings be plentiful and your suffering just enough to amuse the gods.

notes.title: The Deadly Path Beginners Guide Part 2 – The Basics Explained
notes.content:
Greetings, Penitents!

Welcome to the second instalment of The Deadly Path tutorial series. Suppose you’ve just completed the tutorial or are starting your first unguided run. In that case, this guide will walk you through the essential mechanics and gameplay elements to ensure your path through the underworld is as smooth ([i]and deadly[/i]) as possible. Let’s dive in!

[h2]Navigating the UI[/h2]
Understanding the game’s interface is your first step to mastering the path:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44212693/44114bc240aae1b266f5e385b31c705fa26caa79.png[/img]
[olist][*] [b]Population[/b] 
The top number represents the current population of minions.
The bottom number represents the population cap ([i]which can be increased by constructing Hovels[/i])
If population exceeds it’s cap then your upkeep will be increased.
[*] [b]Age[/b]
This represents what age you are currently in and what your technology level is.
Hovering your mouse over this will also remind you which God, Custodian and level you are playing with.
[*] [b]Bones[/b]
[*] [b]Meat[/b]
[*] [b]Gold[/b]
[*] [b]Knowledge[/b]
[*] [b]Blood[/b]
[*] [b]Resurces / Upkeep[/b]
The number alongside Resources represents the amount of that resource that you have.
The number alongside Upkeep is the amount of that resource that will be deducted from your resource pool each cycle.
[*] [b]Resource Info Indicator[/b]
The colour of the skull represents if your production of the relevant resource is less than ([i]red[/i]), equal to ([i]yellow[/i]) or greater than ([i]green[/i]) your upkeep cost.
Hovering over this skull will show a detailed breakdown for the relevant resource.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44212693/fb4523171f0d243f486dd265bacb36de34e4d180.jpg[/img]
[*] [b]Cycles Remaining[/b]
This represents how many cycles are remaining in the current run. You will lose the run if this reaches 0 before completing all objectives.
[*] [b]Cycles until killing moon[/b]
How many cycles remain before the next killing moon event begins ([i]Greater upkeep costs[/i])
[*] [b]XP Bar[/b]
This represents how much XP you have towards your next upgrade/building unlock.
[*] [b]Time left in current cycle[/b]
How much physical time is left for the current cycle.
[*] [b]Game speed / Pause buttons[/b]
Clicking on the pause symbol will pause the game.
Clicking on the arrow will speed up time in game, or reset back to normal time if clicked after reaching the max speed. [/olist]
[h2]The Deadly Path Controls[/h2]
[b]Movement[/b]: Use [b]WASD[/b] or [b]hold the middle mouse button[/b] to move around the map.
[b]Zoom[/b]: Use the [b]mouse wheel[/b] or [b]Q/E[/b] to zoom in and out.
[b]Time Controls[/b]:
[list] [*] Press the [b]space bar[/b] or click the [b]pause button[/b] to pause/unpause the game.
[*] Use the [b]1-3 number keys[/b] or the [b]arrow buttons[/b] to adjust time speed.
[*] [b]Note[/b]: Building on a tile will automatically unpause the game. [/list]
[h2]Excavating Tiles[/h2]
To expand your empire, you’ll need to excavate tiles:
[list] [*] Click on an entombed tile to excavate it.
[*] Excavating costs Meat, and the cost increases the further the tile is from your throne room. [/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44212693/2717b1f239d28c15d1271e6c3295d3eafc26d7d9.gif[/img]
[h2]Extracting Resources[/h2]
Resources are vital to survival and progression. Here’s how to gather them:
[list]
[*] [b]Scavenger Hut[/b]: Extracts Bones ([i]used for constructing new buildings[/i]).
[*] [b]Carving Spit[/b]: Extracts Meat ([i]used for excavation and upkeep[/i]).
[*] [b]Rock Chisel[/b]: Extracts Gold ([i]used to cover upkeep costs of buildings like the Hovel[/i]).
[*] ⚠️ [b]Important[/b]: Resources from tiles are limited! Once a tile is depleted, it will remain empty, so plan your resource management carefully.[/list]
[h2]Assigning Units[/h2]
Efficiently assigning units is key to maximizing resource collection:
[list][*] Drag a [b]unit card[/b] onto a tile to assign it to a building.
[*] [b]Right-click[/b] the tile to unassign the most recently assigned unit.
[*] [b]Shift[/b]: Hold to view all currently assigned units.
[*] [b]Unit Management[/b]: Click on a unit to unassign it from its task. [/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44212693/2ad728a98acac033c01b9a48da59b65c960b1ebb.gif[/img]
[h2]Levelling Up[/h2]
Actions such as excavating, gathering resources, and constructing buildings earn you [b]XP[/b]:
[list] [*] Levelling up lets you choose between unlocking new buildings or upgrading existing ones.
[*] Upgrading existing buildings (e.g., a Carving Spit to extract more Meat per cycle) will apply to all iterations of that building at no additional cost. [/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44212693/09d30ee1bfa0513afb4e6b03d0938ef598084a1d.gif[/img]
[h2]Advancing Through Eras[/h2]
Adjacent to your throne room, you’ll find [b]ERA Beacons[/b]:
[list] [*] Upgrade these beacons to advance through the ages, unlocking higher-tier buildings and expanding your excavation range. [/list]
[h2]Additional Tips and Challenges[/h2]
[b]Killing Moon[/b]: This event increases upkeep periodically. Prepare by managing resources wisely.

[b]Upkeep Costs[/b]: Every full cycle (visible on the cycle countdown on the right of your UI) incurs upkeep costs for your god, buildings, and units. Balance expansion with sustainability.

[b]Manual of Misery[/b]: Press [b]Tab[/b] to access this in-game manual, filled with useful details, tutorials and tips.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44212693/37cc9f255add4c08054cc905829ea15469d5ebbc.gif[/img]

notes.title: Welcome to The Deadly Path: What You Need to Know Before You Begin
notes.content:
Greetings, Penitents!

The gods have spoken, and your journey into the dark, strategic depths of The Deadly Path begins here. Whether you’re a seasoned strategist or new to roguelike adventures, this guide will prepare you to take your first steps as a Penitent and manage your underworld empire.

[h2]What is The Deadly Path?[/h2]
The Deadly Path is a roguelike strategy game that challenges you to balance resource management, strategic planning, and tactical execution as you serve the gods of the Dread Pantheon. Each run presents new challenges, opportunities, and choices that will test your resolve and creativity.

[h2]Your Role as a Penitent[/h2]
As a Penitent, you are tasked with appeasing the powerful gods of the Dread Pantheon and facilitating their return to power. Failure to do so will invoke their wrath - but success could lead to unimaginable rewards.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44212693/37cc9f255add4c08054cc905829ea15469d5ebbc.gif[/img]

[h2]Key Features[/h2]
Here are some of the defining elements of The Deadly Path that make it a unique and thrilling experience:
[b]Roguelike Gameplay[/b]: Every run is a new challenge, with randomized elements and ever-changing strategies.
[list]
[*] [b]Distinct Gods[/b]: Each god offers unique mechanics, requiring you to adapt your playstyle.
[*] [b]Power-Up System[/b]: Utilize powerful boosts to shift the odds in your favor.
[*] [b]Cycle Management[/b]: Time is of the essence - will you use it wisely? [/list]
[h2]How to Start Your Journey[/h2]
[olist]
[*] [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/2463180/The_Deadly_Path_Demo/][b]Download the Demo[/b][/url]
[*] [b]Complete the Tutorial[/b]: Learn the basics of tile placement, cycle management, and surviving the trials ahead.
[*] [b]Play as Roiann, The Blightcaster[/b]: Get your first taste of the unique mechanics each god brings to the table.
[*] [b]Join the Community[/b]: Connect with fellow Penitents in our [url=https://discord.gg/aeqeHm9uEJ]Discord[/url] to share strategies, tips, and progress. [/olist]
[h2]Starting a Run[/h2]
Have you completed the tutorial and are wondering how to start your very first unguided run? Look no further than the following steps!
[list] [*] [b]Press start game[/b]
[*] [b]Choose your deity [/b] (choose the cruel teacher if you need to refresh your knowledge and replay the tutorial)

[h2]Stay Tuned for More[/h2]
This is just the beginning. Over the next few weeks, we’ll be diving deeper into the mechanics, strategies, and secrets of The Deadly Path with a series of blog posts designed to help you master the game.

[h3]Coming Next: Getting Started - The Basics Explained[/h3]
Until then, may the gods guide your steps, Penitents. Your journey has only just begun.

notes.content:
Take a look at the newest god spotlight from The Deadly Path;

will you pledge allegiance to...

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44212693/889ada9fe1bc5c00fab1b172929356a9d0278fba.jpg[/img]

[h2]Plain Text Version:[/h2]
[h3]The Maw[/h3]
A barbaric and highly omnivorous being, The Maw had to be taught to restrain itself by the Mother Of Tears during its early evolution.

Its constant desire to feed caused issues amongst its siblings, who resented having to share living space with its growling stomach and revolting physical presence. 

The ascension to the surface world gave The Maw new hunting grounds in which to carry out its wicked practices. Here, it roamed freely, devouring the foul flora and fauna of Oscurandyth, acre by rotting acre.

It soon began to hunt and feast on the living, once the descendants of the First Crones began to populate the world in earnest. 

For this, and for countless other reasons, The Maw came to be seen as the main evil among the mortal beings of Oscurandyth. It was the god they wanted to expel with the most urgency and contempt, and a large part of their motivation for joining forces with The Low Ones to enact the curse of banishment.

notes.title: God Spotlight: Brass Leviathan
notes.content:
Check out the brand new god spotlight from The Deadly Path;

[h2]The Brass Leviathan[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44212693/a5ed00ed290c775402ca1b0555d7069f734e1854.jpg[/img]

[h3]Plain Text:[/h3]

A [b]gargantuan[/b] being of [b]draconic[/b] and [b]serpentine[/b] qualities, its huge brass scales demonstrate both its physical strength and raw defensive power. Corrupted over time, the [b]Brass Leviathan[/b] wanted merely to slumber in the dark depths of the world’s planetary matter. 

However, its creators, the Most High, had other plans and summoned it to the surface world of [b]Oscurandyth[/b]. Whilst there, it lingered in the cavernous craters and dark recesses of the landscape, [b]carving out continents[/b] with its scaled tail and ferocious jaws. 

However resentful it was of the surface world initially, its fury reached new peaks when it fell victim to the [b]betrayal[/b] of its subordinate gods, the world’s eternal beings and their mortal descendants. 

Condemned to the cave of origination as part of the curse, rather than the abyssal depths from whence it came, the [b]Brass Leviathan’s[/b] rage is perhaps amongst the most deadly and understandable. 

For a being of such size to be physically constricted to suffer in a confined space is [b]unthinkable[/b].

notes.title: Discord Playtest RIGHT NOW! & The One Who Rusts God Spotlight
notes.content:
Following on from our previous successful [b]Playtest[/b], we are jumping right into [b]another one[/b]! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44212693/71597570a44e1582bdefc41754e1e5e6ac873639.png[/img]

We want to give you all the chance to dive right into The Deadly Path and get your hands on our newest available god - [b]The One Who Rusts[/b]. 

You can join our Playtest [b]RIGHT NOW[/b] by joining our [url=https://discord.gg/hcnKRMhyZZ]Discord Server[/url] and checking out the announcement channel for more information. 
The [b]Playtest[/b] will be running for [b]ONE WEEK[/b] only (Ending on the 24th of May).

[h1]The One Who Rusts God Spotlight[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44212693/d8d597d08ca6586ab610b64682c667e2572a14a2.png[/img]

[b]The One Who Rusts[/b] is one of the first deities of The Dread Pantheon known as those Born Of The Most High. A sinister and sombre being, she chose to use her natural creativity by designing and crafting hideous metallic automatons to do her bidding. In the cave, this did not fare well with her siblings, so she was glad of the chance to expand her enterprises once free from the underworld.

[b]The One Who Rusts[/b] took full advantage of [b]Oscurandyth’s[/b] bleak landscape and commanded her minions and a host of the gods of the Minor Pantheon to build her an extensive workshop.
Over the years that followed, [b]The One That Rusts[/b] carried on crafting vicious mechanical followers, seeing The Low Ones as the perfect test subjects for her implements of [b]torture[/b]. 

Her ill-treatment of the Minor gods almost certainly drove them to begin conspiring against the[b] Dread
Pantheon[/b] in earnest. When their betrayal came to fruition and [b]The One Who Rusts[/b] was cursed to return to the cave of origination, her metallic creatures seized up on the spot and her workshop was destroyed. Reawoken from the curse by the presence of the fifth of The First Crones, The Custodian, [b]The One Who Rusts[/b] has her mechanical eye firmly set on vengeance for her imprisonment. 

Regaining her full strength after thousands of years of inertia, she instructs The Custodian to construct a [b]Deadly Path[/b] to the surface of [b]Oscurandyth[/b] as partial penance for the betrayal of their siblings.
A key being in the Dread Pantheon, [b]The One Who Rusts[/b] will stop at nothing to bring The Low Ones to justice. Her aggression and ideas of leadership often infuriate her fellow gods, yet she inspires total dedication and vile admiration from her acolytes and servants.

notes.title: Devlog #1 & Digital Tabletop Fest
notes.content:
[b][i]Our scene opens on a dark ocean as a crash of thunder rends the sky and lightning streaks like skeleton fingers.

Upon a craggy storm-wrecked cliff lies the imposing Fireshine Publishing Castle and Luxury Dungeons.

A shabby, rag-clad figure shuffles down a dimly-lit flagstone corridor to the room at the end where the developers sleep. He is the Custodian. The corridor echoes, but he moves silently, atop a pair of pristine running shoes.

Muttering to himself, he withdraws from his billows a large iron key and opens the door. A sliver of light fills the gloom. The room reeks of rotting food and is heavy with the stench of pestilence. Three lie prone in chains. In front of them a bucket, a scroll and ink. They have been here for a while.

The Custodian shuffles up to Tim - the Lead Developer. He takes out a small notebook, already full of arcane scratchings. He prods the sleeping man with a metal rod on his belt.[/i]
[/b]
Custodian: Tim…it’s time again.

[b]Tim:[/b] (Groggily)...Oh God, no…I just can’t…

Custodian: IT’S IN THE CONTRACT (The walls shake).

[b]Tim:[/b] Ok, Ok, what do you want to know?

Custodian: Tim, the people want to know, how did you come up with the idea for the Deadly Path?

[b]Tim:[/b] If I do this…I want the first turn with the boil lance.

Custodian: Granted.

[b]Tim:[/b] Sick Bastards. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44212693/220523701ec9843e8c07ceda0fbb2cdcb2d51ae7.gif[/img]

You know…it wasn’t always like this. I used to make nice games. For nice people. Where did it all go wrong eh?

A few months ago, I had started playing games like Stacklands, Dome Keeper, Cultist Simulator - nasty games that kill you quickly and make you desperate to play again. It was then I had the thought ‘what about a game where you build a dungeon and protect it.’ You could have timers and cards, but also in real time. It would be like a boiled down RTS management game.

I wanted to make a game that was addictive but brutal - one where you got distracted by pretty things and then it kicked you in the teeth

Custodian: A Dungeon Keeping game…seems familiar.

[b]Tim:[/b] I appreciate that. Dungeon Keeper was obviously a reference, both for setting and style. I’ve always loved dry British humour - Pratchett, Adams. In a way, I try to put it into everything I do…

Custodian: No Meta!

[b]Tim:[/b] Ok! Unlike Dungeon Keeper, I wanted to have no simulations and boil things down to their root nature. Computers are great at simulating, but historically games - particularly board games - are abstracted. For instance Chess doesn’t have real horses in it. I didn’t want imps running around, I just wanted the *idea* of Imps. This is great for indie developers because it means we don’t need to make a thousand animations for one character - just a card and the players’ imagination will do. 

Originally the game was still more complicated - you had building trees, upgrade trees and training wheels. However, these were quickly winnowed to just a few things. 

1. You can excavate a tile
2. You can build on a tile
3. You can place workers in that building.

And that…is it. Everything else flows from this point - you want an upgrade, go up an era, train a servant - make a building and put something in it. It’s a very simple game!

Custodian: It is said that you sacrificed your first systems designer to appease the Dark Lords at the Games Developers Conference.

[b]Tim:[/b] That is unproven. However, it’s a busy market out there and you need to get the edge somehow. And use it.

Custodian: Good, Goood…Right lets get you out of here.

[b]Tim:[/b] Out?!

Custodian: Well, just for a while, we’re going to have you show the game at the Digital Tabletop Festival. Now remember, you’ve got an hour and then its straight back. And…er, don’t mention the boil lance.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44212693/e74c182ce0043fb5505278cec8d9f5eb8c0ed20e.png[/img]
